entries.name: AdminLocation
entries.summary:
Which collection the admin shows, and which document of it is open (by
id); or, with `view: 'assets'`, the asset library (`collection` is then
where the rail goes back to).

members.name: bricks
members.doc: The bricks this site defines.

members.name: collections
members.doc: The site's collections, in the order the sidebar lists them.

members.name: content
members.doc:
Reads and writes. Reads should be uncached, so the admin always shows
what is saved (the app's server functions, or `createContent` in tests).

members.name: previewUrl
members.doc: URL of the app route that renders `<PreviewPage>` from `@mortar-kit/admin/preview`.

members.name: location
members.doc: Where the admin is, when the app keeps it (e.g. in the URL). Without it the admin keeps it itself.

members.name: onNavigate
members.doc: With `location`: called to go somewhere; the app updates `location` (or doesn't, e.g. when its guard says no).

members.name: onDirtyChange
members.doc: Whether the open document has unsaved changes; see `EditorProps.onDirtyChange`.

members.name: resolveLink
members.type: (url: URL) => { collection: string; slug: string } | undefined
members.doc:
Maps a URL of the site to the document it shows, e.g. `/posts/hello` to
`{ collection: 'posts', slug: 'hello' }` (routing is the app's). With it,
⌘/Ctrl-clicking a link in the preview opens that document in the admin;
a link it doesn't map (or without it) opens in a new tab.

members.name: user
members.doc: The signed-in user (`auth.user()` from `@mortar-kit/auth`): shown at the foot of the rail, with Sign out.

members.name: signOutUrl
members.doc: Where Sign out posts. Default `/admin/auth/sign-out`.

entries.name: AdminUser
entries.summary: The signed-in user, as the admin shows them.

entries.name: BrickForm
entries.summary: The form for one entry, from its brick's schema.

entries.name: createEditorStore
entries.summary:
Creates the editor store. It is seeded from `doc()` (normalized, so every
form input has a value to bind; the source is never modified) and
re-seeded if `bricks()`, `collection()` or `doc()` change, e.g. when a
different document is loaded. Edits live in the store until then. The
first entry is selected, or the fields when there is no body.
entries.signature: function createEditorStore(bricks: () => readonly AnyBrick[], collection: () => AnyCollection, doc: () => Doc): EditorStore

members.name: bricks
members.doc: The bricks this site defines.

members.name: collection
members.doc: The collection the document belongs to.

members.name: doc
members.doc: The document to edit. Edits are kept in the editor; a new `doc` value replaces them.

members.name: isNew
members.doc: A new document that was never saved: it starts unsaved, and the first save creates it (the editor then treats it as saved).

members.name: previewUrl
members.doc: URL of the app route that renders `<PreviewPage>` from `@mortar-kit/admin/preview`.

members.name: refresh
members.doc: Bump it after saved content changes elsewhere, so bricks in the preview load again. Saves here do it already.

members.name: onChange
members.doc: Called with a plain copy of the document after every change.

members.name: onSave
members.doc:
Saves the document; without it there is no Save button. Resolve with a
`SaveResult` (e.g. from `Content.save`) to report validation problems,
or reject if saving failed. The editor validates before calling it too.

members.name: onRemove
members.doc: Deletes the document; without it there is no Delete button. The editor doesn't ask first: the handler does.

members.name: onDirtyChange
members.doc:
Called with whether there are unsaved changes, initially and whenever
that changes (only with `onSave`), and with false if the save controls
go away while dirty (the editor unmounts or `onSave` is removed). Use it
to guard in-app navigation, e.g. with the router's `useBeforeLeave`;
closing the tab is already guarded.

members.name: onFollowLink
members.doc:
Called when a same-origin link is ⌘/Ctrl-clicked in the preview (a plain
click selects the brick instead). Default: opens it in a new tab.
`<Admin>` opens the document it points to (see `AdminProps.resolveLink`).

members.name: selected
members.doc: Whose form is shown: an entry's id, FIELDS, or null.

entries.name: EditorStore
entries.summary: The editor's state and the only ways to change it.

members.name: setSlug
members.doc: Sets the document's slug (checked when saving).

members.name: addEntry
members.doc:
Adds an entry of the named brick with its default data at `index`
(default: the end) and selects it. Returns the new id, or undefined if
no brick has that name or the collection has no body.

members.name: removeEntry
members.doc: Removes an entry. If it was selected, a neighbour (or the fields) is selected.

members.name: moveEntry
members.doc: Moves an entry to `toIndex`. Indexes past either end are ignored.

members.name: duplicateEntry
members.doc: Inserts a copy of an entry (new id, cloned data) after it and selects it. Returns the new id.

members.name: setValue
members.type: (target: Target, path: Path, value: unknown) => void
members.doc: Sets the value at `path` in an entry's data or the document's fields.

members.name: insertItem
members.type: (target: Target, path: Path, index: number, value: unknown) => void
members.doc: Inserts `value` into the list at `path`.

members.name: removeItem
members.type: (target: Target, path: Path, index: number) => void
members.doc: Removes item `index` from the list at `path`.

members.name: moveItem
members.type: (target: Target, path: Path, from: number, to: number) => void
members.doc: Moves an item of the list at `path` from one index to another.

entries.name: FIELDS
entries.summary: Selects (and addresses writes to) the document's fields instead of an entry.

entries.name: Path
entries.summary: A location inside an entry's data (or the document's fields).

members.name: url
members.doc: URL of the app route that renders `<PreviewPage>`.

members.name: collection
members.doc: The edited document's collection, by name.

members.name: body
members.doc: Whether that collection has a body. Without one, the preview ignores stored entries, as the site does.

members.name: refresh
members.doc: Bump it after saved content changes (a save, a delete): the preview reloads what bricks loaded.

members.name: selected
members.doc: The selected entry's id, outlined in the preview; null when none (or the document's fields) is selected.

members.name: onSelect
members.doc: An entry was clicked in the preview.

members.name: onLink
members.doc: A same-origin link was ⌘/Ctrl-clicked in the preview (others open in a new tab from there).

entries.name: SignIn
entries.summary: The sign-in page. Render it from the route at `auth.signInPath`.

entries.name: SignInMethod
entries.summary: A sign-in method, as `auth.methods` (`@mortar-kit/auth`) lists it.

members.name: action
members.doc: Path the method's form posts to.

members.name: callback
members.doc: Path an emailed code or link is posted to.

entries.name: SignInParams
entries.summary: The sign-in page's search parameters, as the auth routes set them.

members.name: error
members.doc: Why the last attempt failed: `denied`, `expired`, `invalid`, `invalid-email` or `failed`.

members.name: method
members.doc: With `sent`: the email method that sent it.

members.name: sent
members.doc: The address an email was sent to (if it may sign in).

members.name: email
members.doc: From an emailed link: its address and token.

members.name: returnTo
members.doc: Where to go after signing in.

members.name: methods
members.doc: The ways to sign in: `auth.methods`.

members.name: params
members.doc: The page's search parameters.

members.name: title
members.doc: Heading. Default "Sign in".

entries.name: Target
entries.summary: What a write is addressed to: an entry, by id, or the document's fields.

entries.name: DocMessage
entries.summary: Editor → preview: the full document to render, its collection's name and whether that collection has a body (sent on every change).

entries.name: DocPreview
entries.summary:
A readable preview of any document: its title, its first image large,
then every other field under its label, then `children` (the body).
`<PreviewPage>` shows it for collections without a layout; a layout can
render it too, e.g. around a heading of its own.

members.name: collection
members.doc: The document's collection: its fields' labels and kinds, and its title field.

members.name: children
members.doc: The rendered body, shown under the fields (a collection with a body).

members.name: collections
members.doc: Every collection, to show a reference by its document's title (otherwise its slug).

entries.name: HelloMessage
entries.summary:
Editor → preview: the editor is listening now; answer with `mortar:ready`.
Covers a preview that loaded (and announced itself) before the editor
hydrated, since the iframe is in the server-rendered HTML.

entries.name: LinkMessage
entries.summary:
Preview → editor: a same-origin link was followed (⌘/Ctrl-click) in the
preview. The editor opens the document it points to, if any, or a new tab.

entries.name: PreviewLayout
entries.summary: Renders a document of one collection the way the site does, around its rendered body.
entries.signature: type PreviewLayout = (doc: Doc, body: JSX.Element) => JSX.Element

entries.name: PreviewPage
entries.summary: Renders the document the parent editor posts; empty until the first message.

members.name: bricks
members.doc: The same bricks the editor uses.

members.name: content
members.doc:
Where bricks with `load` read content: use uncached reads, so the
preview shows what is saved now. Without it such bricks show an error.

members.name: collections
members.doc:
The same collections the editor uses. A collection without a layout
then previews as `<DocPreview>`: its title, fields and body.

members.name: layouts
members.doc:
How each collection's documents preview, by collection name: usually
the site's own layout, e.g. a post's title and date around its body.
Without one, a collection previews as `<DocPreview>` (given
`collections`), or else as its body alone.

entries.name: ReadyMessage
entries.summary: Preview → editor: the preview has mounted and wants the current document.

entries.name: RefreshMessage
entries.summary: Editor → preview: saved content changed; data that bricks loaded should be fetched again.

entries.name: SelectMessage
entries.summary:
Editor → preview: the selected entry, by id (null when the document's
fields or nothing is selected), so the preview outlines it.
Preview → editor: an entry was clicked in the preview; select it.

entries.name: mortarKit

members.name: theme
members.doc:
The admin's theme: a theme package's export, as `import midnight from
'@mortar-kit/theme-midnight'` or `require('@mortar-kit/theme-midnight')`
gives it. Without one the admin uses its default look.

entries.name: MortarTheme
entries.summary: A theme for the admin: what a theme package (e.g. `@mortar-kit/theme-midnight`) exports.

members.name: name
members.doc: The theme's name, for messages.

members.name: stylesheet
members.doc: Absolute path of its stylesheet, which sets --mortar-* custom properties on `:root`.

entries.name: allowEmails
entries.summary:
An `authorize` that lets in these addresses, compared case-insensitively;
`*@example.com` lets in a whole domain. Everyone else is refused.
entries.signature: function allowEmails(patterns: readonly string[]): (input: AuthorizeInput) => EmailUser | null

entries.name: allowMembers
entries.summary:
An `authorize` that lets in anyone whose address is in a document of
`collection` (compared case-insensitively). Removing the document locks
them out on their next request. It lists the collection each time, which
suits the handful of members a small site has.
entries.signature: function allowMembers(options: AllowMembersOptions): (input: AuthorizeInput) => Promise<EmailUser | null>

entries.name: AllowMembersOptions
entries.summary: Options for `allowMembers`.

members.name: content
members.doc: Where to look members up: usually the app's `createContent(...)`.

members.name: collection
members.doc: The collection's name, e.g. `'members'`.

members.name: emailField
members.doc: The field holding each member's address. Default `email`.

members.name: nameField
members.doc: A field holding their display name, used over the one the sign-in method gives. Default `name`.

entries.name: Auth
entries.summary: Sign-in for the admin; see `createAuth`.

members.name: methods
members.doc: The methods, for the sign-in page.

members.name: signInPath
members.doc: The sign-in page's path.

members.name: basePath
members.doc: Where the auth routes live (`basePath`), e.g. `/admin/auth`.

members.name: handle
members.doc:
Answers the auth routes (sign-in methods, `POST <basePath>/sign-out`)
and guards `protect`ed paths; null means carry on (the request is
someone else's, or the user is signed in). Call it first in your
middleware: `return (await auth.handle(request)) ?? next();`.

members.name: user
members.doc: The signed-in user (`authorize` asked again), or null.

members.name: require
members.doc:
The signed-in user, or throws a 401 Response (403 for a cross-site
POST). Call it first in every server function that writes: middleware
can't tell which server-function calls are the admin's.

entries.name: AuthError
entries.summary: Why a sign-in failed: the `error` parameter of the sign-in page.

entries.name: authFromEnv
entries.summary:
`createAuth` set up from the environment: the secret, who may sign in,
Google when its client is configured, and email sign-in through Resend
(or your `mailer`). Throws at startup when production is missing a
secret, an admin list or every sign-in method.

entries.name: AuthFromEnvOptions
entries.summary: Options for `authFromEnv`.

members.name: authorize
members.type: (input: AuthorizeInput) => User | Promise<User | null | undefined> | null | undefined

members.name: secret
members.doc:
Signs the session cookie and the OAuth state, and keys token hashes:
at least 32 characters, from the environment, never in code. Several
keys rotate: the first signs, all are accepted.

members.name: basePath
members.doc: Where the auth routes live. Default `/admin/auth`.

members.name: signInPath
members.doc: The app's sign-in page (a route rendering `<SignIn>` from `@mortar-kit/admin`). Default `/admin/sign-in`.

members.name: protect
members.doc: Paths (prefixes) that need a signed-in user; `handle` redirects (GET) or refuses (401) the rest. Default `['/admin']`.

members.name: home
members.doc: Where to go after signing in when no `returnTo` was given. Default `/admin`.

members.name: maxAge
members.doc: How long a session lasts, in seconds. Default 14 days.

members.name: cookieName
members.doc: The session cookie's name. Default `mortar_session`.

members.name: baseUrl
members.doc:
The site's public origin, e.g. `https://example.com`: OAuth redirect
URIs, email links and the same-origin check use it. Set it behind a
proxy, where the request's own URL may be `http://localhost:3000`.
Default: the origin of each request.

members.name: store
members.doc:
Keeps pending email sign-ins. Without it there is no email sign-in.
With the JSON-file store, use a folder outside your content and git
(`createJsonFileStore({ dir: '.data' })`).

members.name: mailer
members.doc: Sends sign-in emails. Default: Resend when RESEND_API_KEY and MORTAR_EMAIL_FROM are set, else (in development only) the console.

members.name: siteName
members.doc: The site's name in sign-in emails.

members.name: methods
members.doc: Methods to offer after the ones from the environment.

members.name: env
members.doc: Where to read variables. Default `process.env`.

members.name: dev
members.doc:
Development mode: a fixed secret, `admin@example.com` as the admin
and emails printed to the console when nothing else is set. Default
Vite's `import.meta.env.DEV`, so a production build never falls back.

entries.name: AuthMethod
entries.summary:
A way to sign in. `createAuth` routes `POST <basePath>/<id>` to `start`
and `<basePath>/<id>/callback` (GET or POST) to `callback`.

members.name: id
members.doc: URL segment and `Identity.method`: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

members.name: label
members.doc: Button text on the sign-in page.

members.name: input
members.doc: What the sign-in page shows for it; see `AuthMethodInfo.input`.

members.name: start
members.doc: The sign-in form was submitted: redirect to the provider, send an email, …

members.name: callback
members.doc: The provider (or an emailed link or code) came back: who is it? A Response instead answers the request as it is (e.g. `ctx.fail`).

entries.name: AuthMethodContext
entries.summary: What a sign-in method gets from `createAuth` for each request.

members.name: returnTo
members.doc: Where to go after signing in: the request's `returnTo` parameter (a path on this site), or the admin.

members.name: sealer
members.doc: The sealer over the app's secret: sign state, hash tokens.

members.name: url
members.doc: Absolute URL of this method's routes: `url()` is its start, `url('callback')` its callback.

members.name: signInUrl
members.doc: Absolute URL of the sign-in page with these search parameters (undefined ones left out).

members.name: allows
members.doc: Whether `identity` may sign in (runs `authorize`), e.g. before sending an email.

members.name: fail
members.type: (error: AuthError, params?: Record<string, string | undefined>) => Response
members.doc: Back to the sign-in page, showing `error`, with these search parameters too (e.g. to keep a code form open).

members.name: redirect
members.doc: A 303 redirect to `location`, setting these cookies.

members.name: setCookie
members.doc: A Set-Cookie header storing `value` for this method (its routes only) for `maxAge` seconds.

members.name: readCookie
members.doc: The value `setCookie` stored, if the browser sent it back.

entries.name: AuthMethodInfo
entries.summary: A sign-in method, as the sign-in page lists it. Plain JSON, so it can cross a server function.

members.name: label
members.doc: Button text, e.g. "Continue with Google".

members.name: input
members.doc: `'button'`: a button that posts to `action`; `'email'`: an email field that posts to `action`, then a code that posts to `callback`.

members.name: action
members.doc: Path the sign-in form posts to.

members.name: callback
members.doc: Path of the method's callback (where an emailed code or link is posted).

entries.name: AuthOptions
entries.summary: Options for `createAuth`.

members.name: methods
members.doc: The ways to sign in, in the order the sign-in page lists them.

members.name: authorize
members.type: (input: AuthorizeInput) => User | Promise<User | null | undefined> | null | undefined
members.doc:
Who may use the admin: the user for this identity, or null if they may
not. Runs when someone signs in and again on every guarded request, so
removing someone takes effect at once; keep it quick (one lookup). The
user is what `user()` and `require()` return; keep it plain JSON if it
goes to the browser. `allowEmails([...])` covers a fixed list.

members.name: secret
members.doc:
Signs the session cookie and the OAuth state, and keys token hashes:
at least 32 characters, from the environment, never in code. Several
keys rotate: the first signs, all are accepted.

members.name: basePath
members.doc: Where the auth routes live. Default `/admin/auth`.

members.name: signInPath
members.doc: The app's sign-in page (a route rendering `<SignIn>` from `@mortar-kit/admin`). Default `/admin/sign-in`.

members.name: protect
members.doc: Paths (prefixes) that need a signed-in user; `handle` redirects (GET) or refuses (401) the rest. Default `['/admin']`.

members.name: home
members.doc: Where to go after signing in when no `returnTo` was given. Default `/admin`.

members.name: maxAge
members.doc: How long a session lasts, in seconds. Default 14 days.

members.name: cookieName
members.doc: The session cookie's name. Default `mortar_session`.

members.name: baseUrl
members.doc:
The site's public origin, e.g. `https://example.com`: OAuth redirect
URIs, email links and the same-origin check use it. Set it behind a
proxy, where the request's own URL may be `http://localhost:3000`.
Default: the origin of each request.

entries.name: AuthorizeInput
entries.summary: What `authorize` receives.

members.name: identity
members.doc: Who the method (or the session cookie) says this is.

members.name: request
members.doc: The request being authorized.

entries.name: AuthSuccess
entries.summary: What a method's `callback` returns once it knows who someone is.

members.name: returnTo
members.doc: Path to go to after signing in, if the method carried one through; `ctx.returnTo` otherwise.

entries.name: consoleMailer
entries.summary:
A mailer that prints each message (sign-in links and codes included) to
the server's console instead of sending it. For development only.

entries.name: createAuth
entries.summary:
Sign-in for the admin. Put `handle` first in the app's middleware and
`require` first in each server function that writes.

entries.name: createLimiter
entries.summary:
A fixed-window counter per key: returns 0 while the key is under `max`
hits in the current window, else the milliseconds until it resets.
Expired windows are swept as it goes, so memory stays bounded by the
clients seen in one window.
entries.signature: function createLimiter(max: number, windowMs: number, now?: () => number): (key: string) => number

entries.name: createMiddleware
entries.summary:
The site's middleware: put it in `start.middleware`. Order: rate limit on
sign-in posts, then `auth.handle` (auth routes, the `/admin` guard), then
uploaded files, then the page (with a CSP) or server function.

entries.name: createSealer
entries.summary:
A sealer over `secret`: one key, or several to rotate (the first signs,
every one is accepted). Each must be at least 32 characters, e.g.
`openssl rand -base64 32`.
entries.signature: function createSealer(secret: string | readonly string[]): Sealer

entries.name: email
entries.summary: Sign in with a link or code sent by email.

entries.name: EMAIL_TOKENS_COLLECTION
entries.summary: The reserved collection pending email sign-ins are stored in.

entries.name: EmailOptions
entries.summary: Options for `email`.

members.name: mailer
members.doc: Sends the sign-in emails. `consoleMailer()` prints them, for development.

members.name: store
siteName
members.doc: The site's name in the email's subject and text. Default: the site's host.

members.name: expiresIn
members.doc: Minutes until a link or code expires. Default 15.

members.name: label
members.doc: Label of the email field's button. Default "Email me a sign-in link".

members.name: id
members.doc: The method's id, in its URLs. Default `email`.

entries.name: EmailUser
entries.summary: The user `allowEmails` signs in.

entries.name: google
entries.summary:
Sign in with a Google account. Add `<baseUrl>/admin/auth/google/callback`
(or your `basePath`) as an authorized redirect URI of the OAuth client.

entries.name: GoogleOptions
entries.summary: Options for `google`.

members.name: clientId
members.doc: OAuth client id (Google Cloud console › APIs & Services › Credentials, type "Web application").

members.name: clientSecret
members.doc: The client's secret: from the environment, never in code.

members.name: hostedDomain
members.doc: Only accept accounts of this Google Workspace domain, e.g. `example.com` (also hints the account picker).

members.name: label
members.doc: Button text. Default "Continue with Google".

members.name: id
members.doc: The method's id, in its URLs. Default `google`.

members.name: fetch
members.type: { (input: URL | RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>; (input: string | Request | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> }
members.doc: For tests: the fetch that calls Google's token endpoint.

entries.name: Identity
entries.summary: Who a sign-in method says someone is.

members.name: email
members.doc: Email address, lowercased. Methods only return addresses they have verified.

members.name: name
members.doc: Display name, when the method knows it.

members.name: method
members.doc: The `id` of the method that signed them in, e.g. `'google'`.

entries.name: Mailer
entries.summary:
Sends email. Implement it over your provider; the sender address is the
mailer's business. Throw if the message wasn't accepted.

entries.name: MailMessage
entries.summary: One email to send.

members.name: text
members.doc: Plain-text body.

members.name: html
members.doc: HTML body, for clients that show it.

members.name: replyTo
members.doc: Where replies go instead of the sender, e.g. the visitor who filled in a contact form.

entries.name: Middleware
entries.summary: A middleware for `start.middleware`.
entries.signature: type Middleware = (event: MiddlewareEvent, next: () => Promise<Response>) => Promise<Response>

entries.name: MiddlewareEvent
entries.summary: What the middleware reads and writes on the request event (`StartRequestEvent` fits).

members.name: nonce
members.type: string | { script?: string | false; style?: string | false }
members.doc: The CSP nonce the page render uses; set here when `csp` is on and nothing set it.

entries.name: MiddlewareOptions
entries.summary: Options for `createMiddleware`.

members.name: auth
members.doc: The site's `createAuth` (or `authFromEnv`).

members.name: blobs
members.doc: Serves uploaded files from this store at the path its `url('')` gives (e.g. `/uploads/`), with `serveBlob`.

members.name: rateLimit
members.doc:
Limits sign-in attempts (posts to the auth routes) per client: `max`
in each `window` of seconds, then 429 with Retry-After. Default
`{ max: 10, window: 600 }`; `false` turns it off. Kept in memory, per
server process.

members.name: clientKey
members.doc:
Who a request is from, for the rate limit; undefined means not
limited. Default: the first address in `X-Forwarded-For`, else
`X-Real-IP`, which a proxy in front of the server sets. Without a
proxy, a Fetch Request doesn't carry the client's address: pass your
own (a shared bucket for everyone would let one client lock every
editor out).

members.name: csp
members.doc:
A Content-Security-Policy for HTML responses. `true` (default) sends
`script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'`,
with a fresh nonce per request that the page render puts on its
scripts; a string is your own policy, where `{nonce}` is replaced by
that nonce; `false` sends none. The server entry must pass the nonce
to `renderToStream` (the plugin's generated entries do).

entries.name: resendMailer
entries.summary:
A mailer that sends through Resend. Throws when Resend refuses a message,
so the sign-in shows an error instead of waiting for an email that won't come.

entries.name: ResendMailerOptions
entries.summary: Options for `resendMailer`.

members.name: apiKey
members.doc: A Resend API key (`re_…`), from the environment.

members.name: from
members.doc: The sender, on a domain verified with Resend, e.g. `'Site <admin@example.com>'`.

members.name: fetch
members.type: { (input: URL | RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>; (input: string | Request | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> }
members.doc: For tests: the fetch to send with.

entries.name: Sealer
entries.summary: Signs, checks and hashes values with the app's secret.

members.name: seal

members.doc:
Sends an entry's form in the background. When present, `<ActionForm>`
stops the browser's own post and calls it; without it, the post goes to
`action(ref)` (where a router may take it over). `islandActions` has it.

members.doc: Stable identifier stored in entries. Lowercase, e.g. `hero` or `feature-grid`.

members.name: label
members.doc: Human-readable name for the admin panel. Defaults to `name`.

members.name: schema
members.doc: The editable fields, built with `fields.*`.

members.name: load
members.doc:
Loads what the brick shows besides its own data, e.g. the latest posts.
Runs on the server when the page renders (pages without JavaScript
included) and in the browser in the admin preview, where it reads
saved content (not unsaved edits to other documents), again after each
save. Read the `data` fields it depends on before the first `await`:
changing those loads again, changing others doesn't. Return plain JSON. Write it before
`component`, so `props.loaded` gets its type.

members.name: action
members.doc:
Handles a post of the brick's form (`<ActionForm>` in its component).
Runs on the server only, through the app's runner (`Content.runAction`),
which reads the entry's stored `data`; what it returns (plain JSON)
reaches the component as `props.submission.result`. Without
JavaScript the post reloads the page with the result; with it, only
the brick updates. The brick's module also reaches the browser, so
take server-only services from `context`, not from imports. Write it
before `component`, so the result gets its type.

members.name: interactive
members.doc:
Runs the brick in the browser (an island) on pages that are otherwise
plain HTML: the page loads JavaScript only when it shows a brick like
this, and only this brick hydrates; the rest of the page stays static.
Its form (`<ActionForm>`) then posts in the background and updates only
the brick. Its `data`, what `load` returned and its latest submission
are sent along in the HTML (plain JSON), and `load` doesn't run again in
the browser. Default false: the brick is server-rendered HTML. Pages
that hydrate as a whole (the admin) render it like any other brick.

members.name: component
members.doc: Renders the brick. Read `props.data.x` (and `props.loaded`, `props.submission`); don't destructure props.

its manual order; an index past either end moves it to that end.
Throws for a collection that isn't orderable, a bad index or an
unknown id. Optional for custom implementations: without it the admin
shows no reorder controls.

the document by id, finds the entry, and calls the action with the
entry's stored (normalized) data. Resolves to what the action returns;
throws when the reference names no entry with an action. Call it from
the app's one server function for brick forms (a plain form post
arrives as URLSearchParams, which becomes FormData; the reference and form
come from the browser: both are untrusted, which is why the data
doesn't travel with them). Optional for custom implementations.

entries.name: isValidAssetKey
entries.summary: Whether `key` is a valid asset key: `<name>-<6 letters or digits>.<known extension>`, at most 100 characters.

entries.name: isValidDocId
entries.summary: Whether `id` is a valid document id: 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-` (a UUID fits).

entries.name: isValidSlug
entries.summary: Whether `slug` is a valid slug: up to 100 lowercase letters and digits, single dashes between (`home`, `about-us`).

entries.name: ListOptions
entries.summary: Options for listing documents. Plain JSON, so they can cross a server function.

members.name: where
members.doc: Keep documents whose `id`, `slug` or top-level field equals each value.

members.name: sort
members.doc:
Order. Defaults to the collection's manual order when it is
`orderable`, otherwise its `sort`; ties are ordered by slug.

members.name: limit
members.doc: At most this many documents: an integer from 1 to 100.

entries.name: MemoryBlobStoreOptions
entries.summary: Options for `createMemoryBlobStore`.

members.name: baseUrl
members.doc: Prefix of `url(key)`. Default `/uploads/`.

entries.name: normalizeDoc
entries.summary:
Coerces unknown data (a stored file, data from props) into a document that
renders and edits safely. A missing or invalid id falls back to the slug,
so hand-written files need none (the next save stores it). With a body,
entries are normalized; without one, stored entries are kept as plain
JSON but never rendered, so turning `body` off loses nothing. A
`position` is kept when it is a finite number. The input
is never modified.
entries.signature: function normalizeDoc(collection: AnyCollection, bricks: readonly AnyBrick[], raw: unknown): Doc

entries.name: normalizeEntries
entries.summary:
Coerces unknown data into entries that render and edit safely: entries of
known bricks get normalized data, entries of unknown bricks keep their
data (as plain JSON), and malformed or duplicate entries are dropped.
entries.signature: function normalizeEntries(bricks: readonly AnyBrick[], raw: unknown): PageEntry[]

entries.name: PageEntry
entries.summary: One brick instance in a body.

members.name: brick
members.doc: The `name` of the brick that renders this entry.

members.name: id
members.doc: Stable id, created once when the entry is added. Never an array index.

members.name: data
members.doc: The brick's data. Rendering normalizes it (`Brick.normalize`); saving should validate it.

entries.name: PageView
entries.summary: Renders every entry with its brick's component. Bricks that load data read `ContentContext`.

members.name: bricks
members.doc: The bricks this site defines.

members.name: entries
members.doc: The entries to render, in order: a page's or a document's body.

members.name: doc
members.doc:
The document the entries belong to. Bricks with an `action` need it:
their forms name the entry by collection, document and entry id, so
the server can read its stored data. Without it, their forms don't post.

members.name: fallback
members.doc:
Rendered in place of an entry whose brick isn't defined (e.g. a brick
that was removed from the code). Default: nothing, which suits a public
site; the admin preview shows a placeholder.

members.name: loadingFallback
members.doc: Shown while a brick's first load is in flight. Default: nothing.

members.name: errorFallback
members.doc:
Shown in place of a brick whose load failed. Without it, the error
reaches the app's own error boundary (a server render fails with it);
the admin preview passes one. It clears when the brick loads again: when
data its loader read before its first `await` changes, or the source's
`track` signal does.

members.name: wrap
members.doc:
Renders around each entry, given its id (stable for the entry's life).
Default: nothing around it. The admin preview marks entries with it, so
a click can find the entry it landed in.

entries.name: referencedCollections
entries.summary: The collections that references in `schema` point to (following objects and lists).

entries.name: referencesIn
entries.summary:
Every non-empty reference in `data`, following `object` and `list` fields,
so a list of references (`fields.list({ of: fields.reference(...) })`) is
found item by item.
entries.signature: function referencesIn(schema: Fields, data: unknown): FoundReference[]

entries.name: Referrer
entries.summary: A document holding a reference, and where. With `entryId`, `path` is inside that entry's data; otherwise it starts with `'fields'`.

entries.name: RemoveResult
entries.summary: Result of `Content.remove`.
entries.signature: type RemoveResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; referencedBy: Referrer[] }

entries.name: RenderedPage
entries.summary: What `createRender` tells the document about the page being rendered.

members.name: hydrate
members.doc: Whether this page hydrates.

members.name: nonce
members.doc: The request's CSP script nonce, if any.

entries.name: RunActionOptions
entries.summary: What the app passes to `Content.runAction` besides the post.

members.name: request
members.doc: The request the post arrived in, passed on to the action.

members.name: context
members.doc: The app's server-side services for actions (see `ActionContext`).

entries.name: sameEntry
entries.summary: True when `value` names the same entry as `ref`: for filtering submissions by entry.
entries.signature: function sameEntry(value: unknown, ref: EntryRef | undefined): boolean

entries.name: SaveResult
entries.summary: Result of `Content.save`.
entries.signature: type SaveResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; issues: DocIssue[] }

entries.name: SchemaOps
entries.summary: What bricks and collections share: defaults, validation and normalization for a record of fields.

members.name: defaults
members.doc: Fresh default data.

members.name: validate
members.doc: Validates (and fills defaults into) unknown data.

members.name: normalize
members.doc:
Coerces unknown data into the schema's shape for rendering: missing fields
get defaults, and fields of the wrong type are replaced by their default.
Values that are the right type but break a rule (an empty required text)
are kept, so a preview shows what the editor typed.

entries.name: serveBlob
entries.summary:
A response serving one stored file: for an app route or middleware such
as `/uploads/*`. Types come from the key's extension and are sent with
`nosniff`, so a file can't be read as anything else; keys never change
content, so files are cached for good. Answers byte ranges (video seeking)
and 404 for an invalid key or a missing file.
entries.signature: function serveBlob(store: BlobStore, key: string, request?: Request): Promise<Response>

entries.name: SortOrder
entries.summary: A list order: by a field of the collection or by slug.

members.name: order
members.doc: Default `'asc'`.

entries.name: Submission
entries.summary: A form post to a brick's `action`, as its component sees it.

members.name: pending
members.doc: True while the post is in flight (only with JavaScript; a plain post reloads the page).

members.name: result
members.doc: What the action returned.

members.name: error
members.doc: What the action threw, if it threw (in production, a generic error).

entries.name: UpdateAssetResult
entries.summary: Result of `Assets.update`.
entries.signature: type UpdateAssetResult = { ok: true; asset: Asset } | { ok: false; message: string }

entries.name: UploadResult
entries.summary: Result of `Assets.upload`.
entries.signature: type UploadResult = { ok: true; asset: Asset } | { ok: false; message: string }

entries.name: useContent
entries.summary:
The content reader for the current component, from `ContentContext`.
Call it in a component body; read with it in a memo (under `<Loading>`).
Throws if no source is provided.

entries.name: validateDoc
entries.summary:
Checks a document before it is saved: its id and slug (not one of the
collection's reserved slugs), its fields against the collection's schema
(issues at `['fields', ...]`), and with a body its entries. Unknown
top-level keys are dropped, and so is `position` (`createContent` keeps
the stored one). Whether the slug is free is the store's
question, not this one.
entries.signature: function validateDoc(collection: AnyCollection, bricks: readonly AnyBrick[], raw: unknown): ValidateDocResult

entries.name: ValidateDocResult
entries.summary: Result of `validateDoc`: the cleaned document, or every issue found.
entries.signature: type ValidateDocResult = { success: true; doc: Doc } | { success: false; issues: DocIssue[] }

entries.name: validateEntries
entries.summary:
Checks entries before they are saved: each entry's shape, unique ids, and
its data against its brick's schema. Problems are pushed onto `issues`
(shape problems at `['entries', index]`); the returned entries have each
known brick's validated data, and entries of unknown bricks are kept as
they are, so retiring a brick never loses content.
entries.signature: function validateEntries(bricks: readonly AnyBrick[], raw: readonly unknown[], issues: EntryIssue[]): PageEntry[]

entries.name: ValidateResult
entries.summary: Result of `brick.validate(data)`.
entries.signature: type ValidateResult<D> = { success: true; data: D } | { success: false; issues: Issue[] }

entries.name: createRender
entries.summary:
The server entry's `render`. Pair it with an entry-client that hydrates
the same tree (`hydrate(() => <Root />, document)`).

entries.name: HydrateOption
entries.summary: Which pages hydrate: all, none, these path prefixes, or a test of the path.
entries.signature: type HydrateOption = boolean | readonly string[] | ((pathname: string) => boolean)

entries.name: hydrateTest
entries.summary: `hydrate` as a test of a path.

entries.name: Render
entries.summary: The server entry's `render`: a stream for pages that hydrate, the settled HTML for the rest.
entries.signature: type Render = (request: Request, context?: StartServerRenderContext) => ReturnType<typeof renderToStream> | Promise<string>

entries.name: RenderManifest
entries.summary: The asset manifest the server entry gets from `virtual:solid-manifest`.

entries.name: RenderOptions
entries.summary: Options for `createRender`.

members.name: manifest
members.doc: `import manifest from 'virtual:solid-manifest'`.

members.name: app
members.doc: The whole document: your Document around your App (with `<ClientScripts />` in its head).

members.name: hydrate
members.doc:
Which pages load JavaScript and hydrate. Default `['/admin']`: the
editor and its preview hydrate, public pages are plain HTML. Prefixes
match whole path segments, case-insensitively (as routers do).
Other pages still load the client entry when they show an interactive
brick (an island), to hydrate just those bricks.

entries.name: stylesOnly
entries.summary:
A copy of `manifest` that resolves to CSS only. Solid's renderer links
every CSS file a rendered module needs and adds a `modulepreload` for
each JS file the client entry imports; `noScripts` drops the scripts but
not those preloads. A build manifest keeps each module's file but folds
the CSS of everything it imports into the module itself and drops the
imports, so nothing is left to preload. The dev resolver answers with the
same CSS and no JS.

entries.name: createFileBlobStore
entries.summary:
A blob store backed by a folder: one file per asset, named by its key
(keys are checked, so none can escape `dir`). Writes are atomic. Serve
the files from an app route or middleware with `serveBlob`.

entries.name: createJsonFileStore
entries.summary:
A content store backed by JSON files. Collection names and slugs are
checked, so neither can escape `dir`. A file that can't be parsed is
skipped when listing (and logged), so one bad file doesn't break every
list on the site, but reading it directly throws.

members.name: dir
members.doc: Directory holding the files, resolved against the working directory. Created on first upload. Keep it out of the app's public folder: serve it with `serveBlob`.

members.name: baseUrl
members.doc: Prefix of `url(key)`: where the app serves the folder. Default `/uploads/`.

members.name: dir
members.doc: Directory holding one folder per collection, resolved against the working directory. Created on first save.
